instruments.notes: Item 7A table labels long put strike 2.948 and short call strike 2.500 (NYMEX-based); note 18 instead gives gas collar floor-ceiling as $2.50 - $2.95, so the table labels look swapped. Fair value shown as $1,342,473 under a header saying dollars in thousands (unit ambiguous; converted treating the figure as dollars). Footnote (b): counterparty option to extend Oct 1 2000 to Jun 30 2001 on 15,000 MMBtu/day at 2.60 floor / 3.08 ceiling is NOT included in table.

Basis differential contracts: spread between NYMEX price and an El Paso/Permian price or Waha West Texas price. Fair value shown as $(212,180) under a header saying dollars in thousands (unit ambiguous; converted treating figure as dollars).

2000 column of oil collar table; weighted average long put 21.47 and short call 17.06 as labelled in Item 7A (note 18 gives floor-ceiling as $17.06 - $21.47, so labels look swapped). Fair value $(2,755,669) is the TOTAL for 2000 and 2001 combined and assumes the counterparty extension is exercised; unit ambiguous (header says thousands); converted treating figure as dollars.

2001 column of oil collar table; weighted average long put 20.48 and short call 16.50 as labelled in Item 7A (note 18 gives $16.50 - $20.48). Period end inferred from footnote (e) extension to June 30, 2001 on 2,500 Bbls/day at 16.50 floor and 20.48 ceiling, a counterparty option; fair value assumes exercise. Fair value reported only on the 2000 row (total of both years).
instruments.evidence_quote:
A counterparty has the option to extend a collar option from July 1, 2000
     to June 30, 2001 on volumes of 2,500 barrels per day at a floor and ceiling
     price of $16.50 and $20.48 per barrel, respectively.
